The design language is genuinely achieved: the resting compositions are finished instruments, the light theme is real ink-on-paper rather than an inversion, ramp directions reverse correctly, amber is rationed, budgets and lexicon bans hold, and mobile captures stay legible -- this does not look like a template. However, the hero's signature entrance choreography is broken by a confirmed CSS cascade bug (the readout delay classes are dead, so the metrics pop in first instead of sixth, without their stagger -- proven by the t=0.3s frame and the liveness capture), one band rail floats alone at t=0, several composition deviations from the binding spec (core-modules 240u row layout, telemetry 224u, hero rail swap, plate bar height) are absent from the deviations ledger that the review contract treats as the only legitimizing record, and the README omits the mandated Active work section. The verdict is FAIL until the motion bug is fixed and the deviation ledger is reconciled; with those addressed this would pass, since the underlying visual system is strong.

confirmedMajors.title: Hero entrance choreography broken: readout stagger delays are dead CSS, rows enter first instead of sixth
confirmedMajors.location: C:\GitHub\hakanduyar\src\hero\hero.ts lines 291-292 (emitted into assets\generated\hero-dark.svg and hero-light.svg style block); evidence .ai\evidence\visual\hero-dark-t0_3s.png and liveness-early.png
confirmedMajors.detail: The emitted CSS declares `.r0{animation-delay:900ms}.r1{960ms}.r2{1020ms}` BEFORE `.ro{animation:rise 240ms ... forwards}`. The `animation` shorthand resets animation-delay to 0s, and since .ro appears later at equal specificity, all three readout rows animate at 0-240ms instead of 900/960/1020ms, and the specified 60ms sibling stagger never happens. The timeline frames prove it: at t=0.3s REPOSITORIES/COMMITS/TYPESCRIPT are fully visible while the header (320ms) and wordmark (480ms) have not started; liveness-early.png shows the real embedding painting three floating numbers in a void as the banner's first content. This inverts the choreography specified in 03-design-brief.md section 6.2 (rows are element #6 at 900ms) and contradicts the implementer's own docs/visual-system.md element order (readouts staggered after the discipline line). The 'instruments report in after the identity' narrative -- the centerpiece of the motion design -- does not happen.
confirmedMajors.recommendation: Emit the per-row delay classes AFTER the .ro shorthand rule, or fold the delay into per-row shorthand rules (e.g. `.r0{animation:rise 240ms var(--ease) 900ms forwards}`). Re-capture the timeline frames and confirm rows appear at 900-1260ms with visible 60ms stagger.

confirmedMajors.title: material-change.mjs skip logic can never skip: clock-derived fields defeat it
confirmedMajors.detail: stripVolatile deletes only capturedAt, but data/telemetry.json contains other purely clock-derived fields: contributions.windowStart/windowEnd (first/last day of the trailing-year contribution calendar, i.e. the run date), activity.start/end (moves one week forward every Monday run), and methods.activity which embeds the end date as a string. Verified against scripts/generate/snapshot.ts (firstDay/lastDay come from the calendar day series, which always ends on the query date) and the committed snapshot (windowEnd 2026-08-23 = capture date). Therefore every scheduled run on a later date compares as a 'material change' even when zero contributions occurred, and the exit-1 skip branch is unreachable in practice. This directly contradicts the script's own header ('If only the clock moved, the refresh workflow skips the commit'), the workflow comment ('A run where nothing moved but the clock produces no commit'), docs/maintenance.md ('commits only if something material changed'), and BACKLOG T-010 AC2. The result is a guaranteed weekly bot commit — exactly the history noise the design says it prevents.
confirmedMajors.recommendation: Strip all clock-derived fields (contributions.windowStart/windowEnd, activity.start/end, methods.activity — or compare only the value-bearing fields: weekly array contents, totals, languages, repos, featured, lastPush) before comparing, and add a test that two snapshots differing only in dates compare as unchanged.

C:\GitHub\hakanduyar\scripts\generate\snapshot.ts queries `contributionsCollection` with no from/to arguments (lines 43-51), so GitHub returns the trailing year ending on the query date. Lines 212-213/223-224 set contributions.windowStart/windowEnd from the first/last calendar day; lines 168-170/237-238 set activity.start/end from the last 52 complete weeks; line 252 embeds activityEnd in the methods.activity string. The committed C:\GitHub\hakanduyar\data\telemetry.json proves it: windowEnd "2026-08-23" equals the capturedAt date "2026-08-23T10:03:00Z"; activity.end "2026-08-22" is the last complete week's Saturday; methods.activity reads "...52 WEEKS TO 2026-08-22".

minors.title: A crash in material-change.mjs is indistinguishable from 'no change' — refresh silently stops forever
minors.detail: The step branches on the script's exit code: exit 0 = changed, anything else = skip. results.summary: I read all binding spec documents, every module under src/, all scripts, workflows and tests, then ran the gates myself: npx tsc --noEmit is clean, all 62 vitest tests pass, `render --check` reports all 18 assets in sync, and `npm run validate` reports 0 errors over 18 assets and 132 manifest strings — the pipeline's determinism design (committed snapshot, fixed 2dp precision, no clocks or locale calls in the render path) is genuinely sound. The verdict is FAIL on one confirmed critical bug: the hero's readout stagger (.r0/.r1/.r2 animation-delay) is dead CSS because the later .ro animation shorthand resets the delay to 0s in the cascade, so the three metric readouts animate at t=0 instead of 900-1020ms, inverting the brief's §6.2 entrance order on the only animated asset — confirmed in the emitted SVG and visible in the team's own evidence screenshot hero-dark-t0_3s.png, and structurally invisible to the existing motion tests, whose regex only reads delays written inside the shorthand. Beyond that, three majors: the snapshot silently truncates at repositories(first:100) with no pageInfo guard (headline count and aggregates would diverge past 100 repos with no error), the validation gates encode ceilings materially weaker than the binding spec (160/700 KB vs the brief's 45-90/400 KB budgets; 10 of 40 build-failing lexicon terms unchecked, all undocumented), and ~290 lines across geometry.ts and motion.ts are dead code that docs/architecture.md and motion.ts's own header present as live architecture. The remaining findings are polish-grade but real: no-op rx on <path> containers (the spec'd 2u radius never renders), 'activity below' pointing the wrong way plus 'Linkedin/Github' casing in generated copy, a refresh guard that conflates crashes with no-change, doc references to three nonexistent test files, and a one-directional drift gate that cannot see orphaned committed assets. Test quality is above average for this kind of project — contrast floors, ramp direction, byte determinism and manifest honesty are real invariants — but the suite has a blind spot exactly where the one real bug lives.

confirmedMajors.title: Hero entrance choreography is broken: the readout stagger delays are dead CSS and the numbers appear first, at t=0
confirmedMajors.detail: The rule string emits `.r0{animation-delay:900ms}.r1{animation-delay:960ms}.r2{animation-delay:1020ms}` BEFORE `.ro{opacity:0;animation:rise 240ms ... forwards}`. The `animation` shorthand resets `animation-delay` to its initial 0s, and because `.ro` has equal specificity (one class) and comes later in the stylesheet, its implicit 0s delay wins the cascade for elements carrying `class="ro r0"`. Verified three ways: (1) the emitted <style> in assets/generated/hero-dark.svg preserves exactly this order after SVGO; (2) CSS Animations spec semantics — a shorthand sets omitted longhands to initial values, and later equal-specificity rules win; (3) the team's own evidence frame .ai/evidence/visual/hero-dark-t0_3s.png shows all three readouts (REPOSITORIES 55 / COMMITS 870 / TYPESCRIPT 64.2%) fully rendered at t=0.3s while the header band (320ms), wordmark wipe (480ms) and everything else are still absent — with 900ms delays working, the readouts would be at opacity 0 at t=0.3s. The binding brief (.ai/project/03-design-brief.md §6.2 row 6) places the instrument rows at 900ms with a 60ms sibling stagger, sixth of nine steps; instead they pop in first, before the frame has even finished drawing, inverting the choreography on the single animated asset the whole system exists to showcase. No documented deviation covers this (.ai/tickets/STATUS.md lists geometry re-derivation only). The test suite cannot catch it: the entrance-ceiling test in tests/scene.test.ts matches only delays written inside the `animation:` shorthand, so standalone `animation-delay` declarations — exactly the broken mechanism — are invisible to it, and no test asserts entrance ordering.
confirmedMajors.recommendation: Move the delays into per-class shorthand rules (e.g. emit `.r0{animation:rise 240ms <ease> 900ms forwards}` per readout, or place the `.r0/.r1/.r2` animation-delay rules AFTER the `.ro` shorthand in the stylesheet). Re-render, recommit assets, and add a test that parses computed per-class effective delays (shorthand-aware) and asserts the brief's ordering: header < wordmark < sub-line < readouts < scale < index < footer.

confirmedMajors.title: snapshot.ts silently truncates at 100 repositories and publishes internally inconsistent numbers past that boundary
confirmedMajors.detail: The query requests `repositories(first: 100 ...)` with no `pageInfo { hasNextPage }` and no guard that `nodes.length` accounts for `totalCount`. At 101+ public non-fork repos (currently 55, historically growing ~12/year), `publicRepos` still uses `totalCount` (correct) while `totalCommits`, the language byte aggregation, `lastPush` and the featured-repo lookup all iterate only the first 100 nodes — the profile would then publish a repository count and a commit/language figure measured over different sets, with zero errors raised. This directly violates the audit's fail-loud ruling (02-audit.md R4: no silent republish of wrong numbers) and the 'no metric without a measurement' rule, because the commit total would no longer measure what its method label claims. Related robustness gaps in the same file: `languages(first: 10)` silently drops byte counts for repos with >10 languages, and `UserPayload.name` is typed `string` though the GitHub API field is nullable — a cleared display name would crash much later inside fontkit layout with an opaque TypeError instead of a clear snapshot error.

minors.title: rx: RADIUS is passed to <path> elements where it has no effect — the brief's 2u container radius never renders anywhere

minors.recommendation: Either bake the 2u radius into the chamferRect path geometry (arc corners) and re-render, or delete the rx attributes and the RADIUS token and record square corners as a deliberate deviation.

minors.title: material-change.mjs conflates a crash with 'no material change', and its skip path is nearly unreachable by design
minors.detail: The script signals 'no material change' via exit 1, but an uncaught exception (JSON parse failure, missing file — it reads 'data/telemetry.json' relative to CWD, unlike every other script which resolves from REPO_ROOT) also exits non-zero. The workflow's `if node ...; then ... else changed=false` therefore treats any crash as 'nothing changed', reverts the snapshot, and reports the run green — a permanently failing guard would silently stop telemetry refreshes forever, exactly the maintenance-decay mode audit ruling R4 exists to prevent. Additionally, the guard's stated purpose ('a run where nothing moved but the clock produces no commit') is almost never exercised on its weekly Monday cadence: the 52-complete-week window advances every week, rotating activity.weekly and changing activity.start/end and methods.activity, so virtually every scheduled run is 'material' even with zero new contributions.
minors.recommendation: Distinguish outcomes explicitly (e.g. print CHANGED/UNCHANGED to stdout and always exit 0, failing the step on any exception; or use exit 0/10 with a `set -e`-safe case statement), resolve the JSON path from the script's own directory, and decide whether calendar-window rotation should count as material — if not, strip activity.start/end and normalize the weekly window before comparing.

minors.title: The drift gate is one-directional: orphaned committed assets pass every check
minors.detail: `render --check` iterates the 18 in-memory builds and verifies each has a matching committed file; it never verifies the inverse — that every .svg under assets/generated corresponds to a current build. If a featured key or asset name changes, the renderer writes new files, the old ones stay committed, `--check` stays green, validate-all still lints the stale files as valid standalone SVGs, and refresh-telemetry.yml's `git add assets/generated` carries them forward indefinitely. The repository would permanently ship dead image files with stale numbers in their <desc> text.
minors.recommendation: In --check mode, also list assets/generated/*.svg and fail on any file not present in the build set (and optionally have the render mode delete unexpected files).

minors.title: Write-scoped workflow uses floating major-version action tags with persisted credentials
minors.detail: refresh-telemetry.yml holds contents:write, persists checkout credentials (needed for its git push), and executes 187 npm packages via npm ci — while referencing actions by floating major tag rather than commit SHA. For ci.yml (contents:read) floating tags on GitHub-owned actions are defensible; for the workflow that can silently commit to the owner's profile README, SHA-pinning is the hardened norm a top-company reviewer would expect. Neither docs/maintenance.md nor docs/github-platform-constraints.md records the pinning choice. Mitigations already present: lockfile with integrity hashes, npm audit clean, GITHUB_TOKEN exposed as env only to the snapshot step.
minors.recommendation: Pin actions/checkout and actions/setup-node to full commit SHAs (with the tag in a comment) at least in refresh-telemetry.yml, or add one line to docs/maintenance.md stating that GitHub-owned actions at major tags is the accepted trust boundary.

minors.title: Scheduled refresh will be silently auto-disabled after 60 days of repository inactivity
minors.detail: GitHub disables cron-triggered workflows in public repos after 60 days without repository activity, and the material-change guard is designed to produce long stretches with zero commits (a run that commits nothing does not count as activity). If the owner pushes nothing anywhere in this repo for two months, the Monday refresh stops silently, and the profile's core honesty claim — 'MEASURED <date>' stays current via weekly re-measurement (maintenance.md: 'Routine: nothing to do') — quietly degrades. Verified: neither maintenance.md nor github-platform-constraints.md mentions the auto-disable behaviour, so it is an undocumented platform constraint for a system whose docs otherwise document platform behaviour meticulously.
minors.recommendation: Document the 60-day auto-disable in docs/maintenance.md with the re-enable path (Actions tab -> enable workflow), and/or have the workflow keep itself alive (e.g. a keepalive commit or GitHub API workflow re-enable step) — several small, standard patterns exist.
